transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-21
Time: 16:00 PDT
Duration: 56 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Lena Ortiz (Redwood SE), James Holloway (Nova Trust - Head AI Ops), Priya Sharma (Nova Trust - Security Architect), Carlos Mendes (Infra Lead), Ellen Park (PM)

Summary:
High-level discovery focused on Nova Trust's requirements for a fully air-gapped, on-prem Redwood Private deployment. Key concerns: offline update mechanisms, hardware constraints (no internet, limited rack space), encryption/KMS and HSM integration, SOC2/HIPAA evidence, audit/logging, and timeline for procurement and pilot. Redwood outlined options for offline packages, USB/sealed media updates, and hardware/quantization tradeoffs.

Topics:
- Air-gapped update process and verification
- Hardware sizing and GPU/accelerator options
- Security controls: KMS/HSM, SSO, RBAC, audit logs
- Networking: no egress, internal-only endpoints, cert management
- Pilot scope and timeline
- Pricing and enterprise support

Action items: (see metadata list)

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya: hey everyone, thanks for joining. i'm maya from redwood, i'm the account lead on this. quick intros?
[00:09] James: yes, james here, head of ai ops at nova trust. we own the infra side for the pilot.
[00:14] Priya: priya, security architect. i'm focused on controls, compliance, and how things get patched in air-gapped sites.
[00:20] Carlos: carlos, infra lead. i'll handle the server install and networking.
[00:24] Ellen: ellen, product, here for success criteria and integration questions.
[00:27] Lena: lena from redwood, i'm the solutions engineer, i'll dig into sizing and the deployment pattern.

[00:33] Maya: quick framing: nova trust has a regulated banking workload that cannot have external network egress. they're evaluating hosted vs dedicated vs private; they've landed on exploring an on-prem air-gapped private deployment. we wanted to understand constraints so we can propose an offline installation path and a pilot.

[00:51] James: right. to be explicit: no outbound internet from the data center. even the update server can't hit public endpoints. all software must be delivered on sealed media or via an approved secure jumpbox that we control.
[01:03] Priya: and from security: we need to ensure cryptographic keys never leave our HSM, and backups must be encrypted with our keys. we also need audit trails for admin activity and model access that are tamper-evident.
[01:15] Lena: got it. we have deployed on-prem for other regulated customers; for air-gapped sites, we provide an "offline bundle" - a signed tarball that contains the runtime, models (or model conversion artifacts), and an installer script. Customers verify signatures using an offline public key we provide; we can also supply checksums and a PGP-signed manifest.
[01:35] Carlos: so the installer runs locally, no need to reach redwood endpoints?
[01:38] Lena: correct, installation is local; telemetries are disabled by default. any telemetry or usage reporting requires explicit opt-in and an external connector which in your case would remain disabled.
[01:47] James: how do we handle model updates? models will need to be updated periodically but only through our internal change control. can we get incremental deltas rather than full model downloads?
[01:57] Lena: good question. we can ship full model artifacts or delta patches depending on the model format. smaller deltas are possible for certain quantized variants, but depends on model architecture. if you prefer, we can provide conversion scripts to re-quantize in your environment so you only bring the conversion artifacts.
[02:15] Priya: important: any process that touches keys must be auditable. does redwood integrate with external HSMs, like Gemalto/Thales or Azure Key Vault HSM modules?
[02:26] Maya: yes, we support KMIP-compatible HSMs and can integrate with on-prem KMS appliances. for some customers we also allow bringing-your-own-KMS where keys never leave the HSM. we'll document key rotation procedures and how the runtime calls into the HSM for decryption.
[02:40] Priya: and what about SSO? we use SAML/AD FS internally.
[02:45] Lena: Redwood's control plane normally supports SAML/SSO, but in air-gapped mode the control plane is a customer-managed instance inside your VPC; it can be configured to point to your AD via LDAP/SAML when reachable. For fully isolated deployments, we recommend RBAC backed by your internal LDAP and local admin accounts for the initial setup.
[03:03] Ellen: from a product perspective, our success criteria: sub-100ms P95 latency for small prompts, throughput for batch jobs, and clear auditability for model outputs used in customer decisions. can we hit that on-prem?
[03:17] Lena: latency largely depends on hardware. for sub-100ms p95 on generation tasks you likely need low-latency GPUs and optimized kernels. we can recommend configurations - multiple 80GB GPUs or A100-like hardware - but if rack space is constrained we can trade accuracy for quantization to run bigger models on fewer GPUs. i'll put together sizing scenarios.
[03:38] Carlos: rack space is the limiter - we have a single 4U slot available in the first site. power and cooling are decent but not datacenter-scale. what do you recommend?
[03:48] Lena: with a single 4U we can support maybe 1-2 smaller inference accelerators or an optimized CPU-only setup for embeddings/smaller models. for larger LLM serving we'd recommend a disaggregated design or bringing in an appliance vendor. Alternatively, we can propose a hybrid: heavy models run in a dedicated on-prem cluster in a co-lo you control, while lighter latency-sensitive models run on the single-rack device.
[04:14] James: hybrid is problematic due to our data residency rules - all inference must occur inside our site. so we need a pure on-site solution.
[04:21] Lena: understood. then we'll focus on quantized models and kernel optimizations. we can recommend 4x80GB-class GPUs if you can expand to two adjacent U spaces; otherwise we can look at NVMe-backed KV cache strategies to reduce memory but you'll see tradeoffs in latency.
[04:38] Priya: about attestation and compliance: we need SOC2 and HIPAA evidence. can you provide those?
[04:44] Maya: yes, we'll share our SOC2 report and our HIPAA compliance summary. note: your on-prem deployment means Redwood's hosted control plane won't have access, so the attestation is for our product engineering and process. we can also provide sample audit logs (anonymized) and a runbook for incident response.
[05:00] Carlos: backups - do you support encrypted backups that can be exported to our tape/air-gapped backup chain?
[05:07] Lena: we support encrypted backups which can be written to a local storage target; the backup packages are encrypted with your keys (KMIP/HSM). They can be shipped to tape or disconnected storage per your process.
[05:17] James: what's the upgrade cadence and how do we approve patches? we have change windows and need signature verification and rollback options.
[05:24] Lena: upgrades are delivered as signed packages; we recommend a test appliance to apply packages first, we provide pre- and post-installation checksums and a rollback image. We also offer an upgrade dry-run script that validates compatibility.
[05:36] Priya: threat model - do any components try to phone home for license validation?
[05:40] Maya: in air-gapped mode there is no outbound phone-home. License validation can be done via signed tokens that you validate locally; or via periodic offline license files issued by us and signed cryptographically. we can accommodate your internal license attestation process.
[05:54] Ellen: can we run internal benchmarks? we need to reproduce latency/cost numbers ourselves.
[05:58] Lena: absolutely. we'll provide a benchmarking harness and a dataset subset you can run offline. we'll help schedule a bench window and be on the call to interpret results.
[06:07] James: timeline - procurement for new hardware will take 4-6 weeks, procurement freeze windows are important. we'd like a pilot inside 8-10 weeks if possible.
[06:15] Maya: that aligns with other customers; we'll aim to deliver a pilot plan that fits. initial pilot could be a small inference surface with one or two models and can be expanded.
[06:23] Carlos: cost question - how do you price on-prem? is it perpetual, subscription, or support-only?
[06:29] Maya: options: annual subscription for software + support, or a perpetual license plus annual support/updates. pilots typically run on a short-term subscription and convert to enterprise terms. i'll include ballpark numbers in the follow-up.
[06:39] Priya: any known limitations with specific HSM vendors? we've had issues with vendor X in the past.
[06:44] Lena: we support KMIP and common HSMs; for anything proprietary we'll run a quick compatibility test. we do have customers using Thales/Entrust/Gemalto successfully. we'll document integration steps.
[06:56] James: excellent. last question: what happens if we need emergency patches after an incident? we can't just accept a cloud-pushed hotfix.
[07:04] Maya: emergency patches are delivered as signed offline packages; we can coordinate a special change process and provide a hotfix bundle with verification steps. we also offer a remote assistance plan where an engineer can connect via an approved jumpbox under your control for guided installs - only if you permit it.
[07:22] Ellen: ok let's recap next steps verbally.
[07:25] Maya: sure - redwood to share air-gapped runbook, SOC2/HIPAA docs, and benchmarking harness. lena to provide HW sizing options and quantization tradeoffs. we'll propose pilot scope and pricing.
[07:36] James: we'll confirm hardware procurement timeline and security constraints and share the list of approved vendors.
[07:41] Priya: we'll share KMS/HSM policies and any SAML/AD connectivity docs.
[07:46] Carlos: i'll prepare the rack spec and power/cooling details.
[07:49] Maya: great. thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the materials and schedule the benchmark window.
[07:55] (call ends)

Notes about transcription: occasional misattributions and truncated words; some technical terms like KMIP, KV cache, and HSM occasionally transcribed as km-ip, k v cache, etc. Natural speech present (ums, yeah).
